notes: Yamamoto-first discovery pass completed after rereading the current durable docs/PRIORITIES.md, docs/EDITORIAL.md, docs/DOMAINS.md, and radar/inbox/README.md. Fresh checks of Jazz House ALFIE, BODY&SOUL, current Tsuyoshi Yamamoto schedule traces, Space M&A, and credible Japanese-jazz sources did not reveal a new verified, unrecorded Yamamoto appearance. Blue Note Tokyo's newly visible January 2027 schedule produced two unrecorded projects that clear Stage 1 on specific musical context rather than venue prestige. Jeff Parker's ETA IVtet is admitted for the long-running quartet's minimalist, electronics-inflected, form-bending improvisational language around the current Happy Today project. The Messthetics and James Brandon Lewis are admitted for a specific DMV-to-Tokyo thread: the Fugazi rhythm section of Brendan Canty and Joe Lally, Washington guitarist Anthony Pirog, and Lewis fuse post-hardcore rhythmic identity with improvising saxophone in a working quartet. Stage 2 assigns A+ throughout. Parker has six Blue Note Tokyo sets across three days, while the Messthetics/Lewis project has six Tokyo sets across Blue Note Tokyo and COTTON CLUB and is documented as a heavily touring working band; in both cases A+ fully captures 'actively make room' without manufacturing S-level scarcity. Recent/current RADAR sanity checking did not create a reason to inflate these multi-set engagements into S or S+. Proposed batch shape: A+ 3, A 0, S 0, S+ 0.

en.why_it_matters: The draw is the band's method, not Parker's résumé. ETA IVtet grew out of years of weekly sessions in a tiny Los Angeles room, developing a language in which guitar loops, saxophone tone, bass pulse and Bellerose's loose percussion can stretch a groove until composition and improvisation stop feeling like separate things. Happy Today carries that language forward, and hearing the exact quartet at close range in Tokyo is a strong match for Listening Notes' interest in instrumental identity and music that builds form in real time.
en.trip_verdict: Actively make room for one set if January overlaps with Tokyo. Six sets across three days make Aoyama easy to fit around a larger Kanto itinerary, so choose the performance that fits best rather than sacrificing a genuinely singular one-night event elsewhere.

es.why_it_matters: Aquí importa el método de la banda, no el currículum de Parker. ETA IVtet nació de años de sesiones semanales en un cuarto diminuto de Los Ángeles y desarrolló un lenguaje donde los loops de guitarra, el timbre del sax, el pulso del bajo y la percusión suelta de Bellerose pueden estirar un groove hasta que composición e improvisación dejan de sentirse como cosas separadas. Happy Today lleva esa gramática hacia adelante, y escuchar al cuarteto exacto de cerca en Tokio encaja de lleno con el interés de Listening Notes por la identidad instrumental y por la música que construye forma en tiempo real.
es.trip_verdict: Sí le haría espacio activamente a uno de los sets si enero coincide con Tokio. Seis funciones en tres días permiten acomodar Aoyama dentro de un itinerario mayor por Kanto; escogería la que mejor embone sin sacrificar un one-off verdaderamente singular en otra parte de la región.

events.factual_description: Blue Note Tokyo presents The Messthetics and James Brandon Lewis on Thursday, January 21, 2027, with sets at 6:00 PM and 8:30 PM. The lineup is Brendan Canty on drums, Joe Lally on bass, Anthony Pirog on guitar and James Brandon Lewis on saxophone. Blue Note Tokyo identifies Canty and Lally as the Fugazi rhythm section and describes the collaboration with Lewis as beginning after Pirog invited him to perform with the trio in 2019; the group released its first collaborative album in 2024 and the follow-up Deface The Currency in 2026. The venue lists a music charge of ¥8,800 and also identifies January 22-23 COTTON CLUB dates as part of the same Tokyo visit. Jam Session member reservations are scheduled to open September 11, 2026 and general web reservations September 18, 2026.

en.why_it_matters: This is a particularly clean Listening Notes crossover: Canty and Lally bring the rhythmic memory of Fugazi, Pirog brings the exploratory guitar language of Washington's experimental scene, and Lewis does not sit on top as a jazz guest so much as push the whole quartet into a different improvisational vocabulary. In Tokyo, that makes the concert both a hard-edged instrumental event and a small piece of DMV musical culture traveling intact rather than a generic jazz-rock booking.
en.trip_verdict: Actively make room for one Tokyo set if the January dates overlap with the trip. Aoyama is the first door into a three-day run, but the following COTTON CLUB dates mean there is no geographic reason to force this particular night if another scarce Kanto event conflicts.

en.why_it_matters: The quartet is the event: Fugazi's Canty-Lally rhythm section, Anthony Pirog's Washington experimental-guitar vocabulary and James Brandon Lewis's muscular tenor language have become a real working band rather than a collision of résumés. The current music lets punk economy, groove and open improvisation coexist without sanding off their differences, and the DMV lineage gives the Tokyo appearance an unusually specific cultural connection for Listening Notes.
en.trip_verdict: Actively make room for one of the Marunouchi sets if January overlaps with Tokyo, especially if the Blue Note date does not fit. Treat the three-day city run as alternate access to the same strong project; there is no need to see multiple sets or displace a truly singular Kanto night.
